title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-06-07
lineage: MR > DAT > CD > EAC > Cool Edit 96(Resampled to correct pitch) > SHN > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rare Janis‑Joplin guest spot and classic ’69 Dead fire make the show shine despite a hissy, low‑fidelity soundboard source.
ai_review.review: The performance is legendary – Lovelight with Janis Joplin, a scorching Dark Star, blistering Eleven and the first ever Dire Wolf are repeatedly singled out as highlights.  The recording is a soundboard (SBD) that suffers from hiss, limited dynamic range and apparent mixed‑source inconsistencies, especially on Me & My Uncle, but fans consider it worth owning for its historical value.

ai_rating.rationale: Average user rating is >4.3; the show receives strong praise while the audio quality draws consistent complaints, yielding a high‑overall score with solid confidence from many reviews.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hissy tape with very low dynamic range; some tracks sound like they come from different generations (digital static on Me & My Uncle, analog‑warm Lovelight). Reviewers note multiple source material and a lack of crispness.

standout_songs: Sittin' on Top of the World
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early acoustic‑flavored numbers give way to a high‑energy second set; the Dark Star and Eleven provide the classic ’69 fire, while Lovelight with Janis serves as the unforgettable climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for fresh, nimble soloing and beautiful tone – especially on Me & My Uncle and during the Lovelight duet.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned only in a recollection about backstage apple juice; no specific performance comments.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten (TC) noted on keyboards, providing solid organ work throughout.
